Far Cry 5 is a decent entry into the series, and often underrated in comparison to previous titles.

Honestly, if you played Far Cry 2, 3 or 4 - you know what to expect. Same game, different setting. The main reason people rate it lower than 3 and 4 is because by this point, they've grown tired of the same old formula (and because of the weird ending, but I'm not gonna spoil that... you have to see it for yourself). Far Cry 5 is just as good as its predecessors. That said, let's give this a proper analysis, shall we?

[h1]You shoot bad guys. This time it's in rural America.[/h1]

It's a Far Cry game. What did you expect? It follows the Ubisoft open world formula of a big world occupied by enemy forces, which you slowly liberate by wiping out enemy outposts like you're goddamn Rambo. There's a basic but functional stealth system of silent melee takedowns, silent weapons like bows, throwing knives, and silenced guns, and enemies raising the alarm if they see you or find a dead body. You can conquer outposts either by going in slow and methodical, or you can just storm in guns blazing and mow everyone down with an MG. The combat is fun. Controls are pretty smooth, most weapons are satisfying to use, and neither you nor the enemy are bullet sponges. Sometimes you will have to deal with enemy helicopters, or you can fly one yourself to rain death from above. Fun!

The only criticism I have compared to earlier Far Cry titles (especially Far Cry 1 and 2) is how the physics engine has been dialed down a bit. Many items are static objects that don't ever move (I kicked a bunch of cans and they just stayed in place... lame), and most cover can't be pierced by bullets, unlike earlier games where thin wooden walls could easily be penetrated by high caliber weaponry. At least the fire spreading mechanics are still there, making the flamethrower a potentially devastating weapon... with which you can easily grill yourself if you're not careful.

The game is set in Hope County, a fictional area in the US state of Montana, where a crazy cult is taking over and forcibly recruiting the population. You arrive as a policeman (or policewoman, this is the first Far Cry game with character customization and you get to pick your gender) coming to arrest the leader of that cult, but of course the cultists fight back and you have to run. During the course of the game, you meet with various resistance members and help them fight the cult until they are wiped off the map. The setting is quite enjoyable, especially if you like rural America. As a European, I find American culture quite fascinating, and this game is full of it. All the resistance people are proud American patriots, and you get to see a lot of those weird roadside attractions they have in the rural US, like a park with giant plastic mammoth statues and farms that advertise their tomatoes with giant tomato signs. Very quaint.

[h2]I got captured... AGAIN[/h2]

As far as the story structure is concerned, the antagonists are pretty interesting and the story overall is competently told. But the way they force you into the main quest missions... yeah, that's definitely [i]questionable[/i]. Whenever you earn enough "Resistance Points" in a region (by doing side quests or liberating outposts), the bad guys will send a capture party to abduct you. They don't just do it once per region, but several times. When I finished the game, I had been captured at least six times... and if we count the scenes where Faith puts you into a drug-induced trance so she can try and convert you to the cult, that increases to nine times.

Nine. Times.

And each time, you - of course - manage to escape and kill a whole bunch of cultists in the process. They should have realized that keeping you alive is a bad idea after the second time, but nope. They just keep abducting you and try to convert you to their cause, until you finally kill all the leaders. Of all the methods they could have used to drive the story forward, this is by far the dumbest. It almost feels like the bad guys are deliberately giving you a chance over and over again.

The cult leaders are appropriately vile and violent characters, and the acting and animation is really good. I usually hate cutscenes, but I found the ones in Far Cry 5 to be quite engaging, because the characters are so interesting. I have to rate the main story as "good", but... the way they keep using that abduction mechanic to drive the plot forward... that's just stupid. So utterly stupid. And the worst part is that it can hit you anywhere once you triggered it. Doing a sidequest right now? Haha sorry, abduction squad is here. Flying around in a helicopter? Yeah there's a sedative arrow in your leg now, don't ask where it came from. It's just dumb.

[h3]You've seen it before. It's nothing new, but it's good.[/h3]

Really, apart from the dumb way they handled the main story progression with those stupid abduction scenes, Far Cry 5 doesn't bring anything new to the table. It's another competently made Far Cry game. More of the same for people who enjoy this style of game. Open world driving around, shooting bad guys, doing side quests. It even has the same mission types as the previous Far Crys: rescue a friend and man the gun while he drives the truck to your home base, go to a location and kill the enemies, find collectibles and bring them to an NPC, etc etc. The standard fare as usual. Did you play Far Cry 3 or 4? This is like that, except set in Montana instead of a tropical island or Tibet.

If you like Far Cry games, you're gonna like this. If you don't, you won't. Simple as.

I've been a fan of Far Cry since the 3rd game, and was pretty excited for this one. I was not disappointed for the most part. As a fan of the series I have a lot to say about this game, so be preprared for a long read.

PROS

+ Looks amazing and is well optimized

+ Soundtrack is great, including the radio songs

+ Joseph Seed, the antagnoist, while not as good as Vaas or Pagan Min, is still good and really feels intimidating.

+ Enemies actually have motivation and purpose, as opposed to the mindless pirates in FC3 or the braindead soldiers in FC4

+NPCs have stuff to say now, they can tell you about locations, bases, hidden stashes, etc. Some even have conversations with each other that are fun to listen to, huge improvment from the old NPCs who were basically just there to be eaten by animals. The main NPCs are great and memorable too.

+Lots more wildlife than the previous games, even have challenges to hunt them

+Fishing is cool I guess, it's actually engaging and not an AFK activity like fishing in most games

+ Planes and Helicopters are now in the game, and you can buy and customize vehicles instead of having to find them

+ The bosses besides Joseph are more fleshed out and have their own methods and personalities.

+ Companions are a new addition and are great, they never feel like a burden and can be instructed. Peaches is my personal favorite

+ New resistance system is cool, you complete lots of varied activities in the world until you have enough points to face the regional boss and liberate the region.

NEUTRAL

~ I'm personally not a fan of the setting, I live in the U.S. so Montana isn't all that intersting to me, I'd much rather travel somehwere far away and exotic, however they do pull it off well, the atmosphere is great and I can see why people love it

~ Co-op is an absolute blast however friends can't progress with you, you have to do each person's game twice

~ Arcade is meh and most of the maps are player made and suck. Wish you could choose to only play Ubisoft maps

CONS

- Hunting only yields you money, gone are the days of crafting upgrades, which is a huge shame, the old system was much more engaging.

- Weapon variety is pretty bad, most weapons are just reskins of the same gun, even the unique weapons are identical to the standard versions, and they don't require anything to unlock, just more money, which is strange because the standard weapons are locked until you get enough resistance points, you can get the unique AKM before the standard one, it makes no sense at all.

- Perks feel underwhelming compared to previous games.

- Enemy planes and helicopters spawn way too often, feels more like a chore to kill them rather than and exciting battle.

-No bladed melee weapons, I miss cutting people up with my machete/khukuri :(

-Microtransactions for skins. Why was this necessary? It doesn't even cost much to unlock things with in-game money.

Overall I think the game is good and definitely lives up to the Far Cry franchise, there are issues that bug me but they didn't ruin my experience. I think you'll enjoy this game, it's worth the full 60$, something that can be seldom said about games in this industry nowdays.

[h1]In a nutshell:[/h1]
[u]Pros:[/u]
1. Good graphics
2. Surprises in the story at the end
3. Game physics is good
4. More involvement of Bosses in game (unlike Far Cry 4), which is good.
5. Adds lot more contents in the game when compared to its predecessors.
6. Availability of Guns for hire. OR form Your own squad with AI characters, which gets unlocked as the story progress.
7. No more tower capture to unlock a region (although some elements of it exists here too)
8. More detailed and realistic gun/vehicular battles.
9. Support for Co-op in Story mode.
10. Arcade mode for some extra game play.

[u]Cons:[/u]
1. Even on pretty good configuration PC(GTX 1070 8GB), FPS drops to 30 sometimes, but not many instances. Probably because the game is tailored for AMD graphics.
2. No option to change difficulty in middle of game story. Need to play out entire story in same difficulty level.
3. Too much content in Game User Interface (UI) /Map which causes the UI to be cluttered.
4. If You are someone who is moving up the far cry timeline and played FC3 and FC4 before this, You might take at least an hour of game play to understand the game features.
5. In gun battles, hit reg not accurate sometimes.
6. Co-op in story mode restricted to only 2 players in total (i.e. Yourself and one friend).
7. If You invite Your friend to play in Co-op, only Your story proceeds/missions complete, and your friend's does not. 

Above Pros and Cons should be sufficient if You do not have time to read through the detailed review and need to decide if You want to buy this game or not. More detailed review below.

P.S: Please play this game before playing Far Cry: New Dawn, to enjoy the new dawn instalment better.

[h1]In Detailed Review:[/h1]
[u]The Game:[/u]
Unlike prior Far cry instalments, this game environment has more modern vibes to it. So, You'll have more modern weapons, and visiting a place on the map reveals it. No more tower climbing to remove cloaking.

Basically, the map is a group of islands, ruled over by one main Boss (The Father) and 3 under bosses (His 2 brothers and 1 sister, well not biological though, haha). They together form a cult and make life hell for the natives. Its either join the cult or face Your maker, simple right?

So, You play the role of a rookie deputy who will fight Your way to liberate the islands, and there is lots of story and elements to it on the way.

[u]The bosses:[/u]
Each boss brings in their own flavour and elements to the story and game play, which is kind of good and makes missions less repetitive. The more outposts You liberate (not many, may be 4 to 5 outposts per boss) and more missions You complete (given by the natives), the more interest the local boss takes in You, taking you closer to defeat them.

[u]The Vehicles:[/u]
A wide variety of Vehicles available, like trucks, vans, SUVs, boats etc along with the new addition of airplanes and helicopters, which can be used in free roam and missions.

[u]Guns for Hire:[/u]
Basically 2 types:
Type 1: Civilian
Each civilian You rescue from the cults grasp during free roam can be used as a Gun for hire during next mission, until You release them. They ride with You, they can die for You, kill for You with guns blazing or with stealth. They can be found all over the map. No specialisations as such, good for regular gun fights.

Type 2: Story AI Characters
The other set of Guns for hire are the characters which are unlocked as You progress in main story. This set of Guns for hire are specialists and can be added to your squad. They can be called upon whenever You need them. There are 9 of these specialists which includes 3 animals and rest humans. The human specialists include a sniper, an airplane pilot, a helicopter pilot, a crossbow specialist (for stealth), a missile man etc. You can form a squad with them or call them in separately.

[u]Skills:[/u]
Unlike prior instalments, skills in FC5 can be unlocked by finishing challenges. The challenges (which can be viewed in Map menu) needs to be completed to get reward points. These reward points can be used to unlock skills. Some challenges (for example) are get 10 kills with grenade, 8 kills with knife throw, 20 Melee kills, 5 road kills etc. So, higher the game difficulty, completing some challenges might get a bit difficult as game AI gets better.

Skills are similar to FC3 and FC4, not many changes here. One difference I noticed is, no more crafting for weapon bag, loot bag, weapon holster etc by hunting animals for skins. This too needs reward points now. So make sure where You spend Your reward points well.
  
[u]Weapons:[/u]
Anything and everything from a knife to arrow, pistol to assault and sniper rifles, from Grenade launchers to guided RPGs. If You have DLCs purchased too, You get martian weapons as well. You can carry upto 4 weapons at a time, provided You have unlocked the large weapon holster by using those reward points.

Overall I would definitely recommend the game.

I'm giving this a good review because I liked it and plan to play through it again for giggles, but I'm going to start by saying I don't think everyone will enjoy this.  Here's why I liked it:

1.  Shooting mechanics are pretty tight and intuitive.  I know that's really basic, but if it's off in a FPS that just kills it for me.

2.  I love the premise.  This setting and the idea of this game just jives with me.  I'm fascinated by prepper culture and cults.  Riding around in a pickup truck shooting guns at a bunch of psychos with my redneck buddies is just my idea of a good time.

3.  They actually tried really hard to give this game personality.  Thing is there's not a lot of acting in the game, it's not an RPG, but what's there is really solid.  They took great pains to make it really look like Montana.  You will hate the villains and you will like the good guys (Poor Jess!); they did a lot with very little.  Also the soundtrack of this game is freaking amazing, and it looks really good.

4.  I'm a working adult, I like games I can play for 20 minutes and get something done.  I also like story driven FPS.  This works for me.

Here's why I think other people wouldn't like it:

1.  Very, very loose approach to the narrative.  If you are one of those people who loses interest in a show when the characters do something that doesn't strictly make logical sense, or you lose your mind when you encounter a plot hole, you're going to hate this.  If you can just kick back and say "it's just a game", or make up the reasons in your head why something happened, (i.e. you have a strong suspension of disbelief like I do) you'll be okay.  But a lot of things happen that just don't make any sense, if that bothers you, you won't like it.

2.  The multiplayer aspects didn't thrill me, though I like the Arcade feature, that one's good, the rest... meh.

3.  The bullet drop with sniper rifles drives some people crazy.

4.  A friend of mine who tried this thought it was more like an RPG, and while it has a few light RPG style elements, it's not an RPG.  It's a shooter with some character customization.

I highly recommend you buy it on sale, even if it sounds good to you.   I mean I've played more money for worse games, but at least this way if you don't like it you're not out too much.

If you've liked the previous games in the franchise, you''ll like this one as well. It does have the typical "do the missions, get your upgrades", but there is a different, more refined feel to me.  The world looks beautiful.  I have a pet.  I have a plane.  I have a gun.  All is going according to God's plan.

[H1]Pros:[/h1]

+ Gameplay is a blast, they've definitely stepped up things from the last two. Throwing shovels at people is the funnest thing this game brings to the table.
+ Setting is very interesting, the expansive American area is a jarring difference from the first two games and the area is beautifully rendered. 
+ Graphically impressive.
+ Some of the characters are interesting or hilarious to interact with, with the game finding (not so subtle) ways to reference old games and current culture.
+ Co-Op system is interesting and fun to screw around with, as is the hiring system.
+ Arcade and build editer can add numerous hours to the people who enjoy that sort of thing.
+ While the game includes microtransactions, they are inexplicably so easily overpassed that I'm confused what Ubisoft is thinking. You can easily find enough bars to unlock skins, and ultimately the skins are useless unless you enjoy Arcade.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]

- The story is literally the worst in the series, in a series that has never been particularly strong in storytelling. I'm going to have to break this down into parts, as this factor alone is enough to make me mad:
[list]
[*] The kidnapping mechanic gets extremely old quickly and requires a significant suspension of disbelief because A. even though you're doing terrible shit to these people, they STILL basically spare you, B. they can reach you no matter what is happening, and C. the drugs they use to do this basically have no fucking rules and can be used to control, capture, or drive crazy seemingly interchangably. 

[*] Speaking of drugs, the Far Cry series needs to let go of this absurd erection they have with mind altering substances. It was a neat novelty in 3 with the fight with Vaas, but ever since they've insisted upon keeping it going as a running theme. 5 simply takes this way too far. One single drug that can turn you into a sleeper agent, turn you into a stupified zombie, turn you into a murdering maniac, and somehow turn you completely to Joseph's entire cause in a second. Bliss acts literally any way the developers want it to: it serves as the major way a lot of the conflict starts in the story. 

[*] While games don't always have to have a voiced protagonist, there is a significant downfall in not having one in this game. Cutscenes feel like they're looking for a response and end up suffering in awkward silence. Characters have intense breakdowns (some of which you shouldn't even be able to see and it's never elaborated on why you can see it) and your character stands there blankly, only occassionally nodding or shaking his head.

[*] I hate how every Far Cry game feels like it has to have a 'moral dillemna' ending, because the lead writers keep displaying how inept they are at creating one. Every bad guy questions if you're doing the right thing, calling you a monster and a hypocrite. The main bad guy does this as well, insisting that every bit of suffering is by your doing. This would work if there was any footing to stand on, such as the cult never killing but instead capturing at every opportunity. This is not the case. You can find bodies tortured to death around the entire area, people murdered for being 'weak', etc etc. Any power of the antagonists calling you out falls flat and feels pointless.

[h1] The following is about the ending of Far Cry 5 [/h1]

[*] [b] (SPOILERS AHEAD) [/b] Speaking of a moral dilemma ending, the ending to Far Cry 5 is the worst ending I've ever had the misfortune of experiencing. You are given two options: Leave the Father with inexplicably instantly hypnotized friends, or resist to the downfall of all involved. Resisting is arguably the canon ending and after a dumb 'boss fight', guess what? Nuclear explosions detonate in the landscape (possibly by Joseph's hands), and after everyone is dead but you and him, he happily and smugly says he's right and you're his son now, to help bring in the new world once the smoke clears.

[*] [b] (SPOILERS AHEAD PART 2) [/b] It's clear that the game intends to make the question: If Joseph is actually right, then aren't we the bad guys? The problem with this is that Joseph still has no leg to stand on: he's a mass murdering, abusive lunatic who (with his family) kills entire communities who slight them. There is no possible way to flip this around as "Joseph's actually a good misunderstood guy trying to save people". So why does that matter? There is no satisfaction in this ending: if Joseph was right and we were ACTUALLY the bad guy, we'd have something like Bioshock or Spec Ops: The LIne's ending. But Joseph isn't right. And instead of bringing him to justice, bizarre circumstances (that he likely caused) destory any semblance of closure the player can hope to have. This is particularly irritating because the promotional descriptions talk about liberating the area, which I was very happy as it occured each time -- only for it to entirely be useless, regardless of what ending you choose.

[*] [b] (SPOILERS AHEAD PART 3) [/b] Endings don't have to be positive: terribly depressing and "you were the bad guy" endings can be fantastic. But it feels like Far Cry 5 tried to have its cake and eat it too: trying desperately to look as though it has depth but lacking any. There is no significant moral lesson to be learned or considered, no aspect of humanity to question. The antagonists are not relatable nor are they particularly interesting or flawed. The main character has no voice to contribute to any conversation nor is he ever in the wrong outside of what the cultists do or make him do. 

[*] [b] (SPOILERS AHEAD PART 4) [/b] I think what ultimately makes these endings so annoying is that they're completely interchangeable. You could drop a nuke at the end of most videogames with a bad guy and have the same amount of depth to it. It's a copout, someone desperately trying to make an ending fatalistic without putting any work into it.


[/list]

- The difficulty to this game is bizarre. Sometimes you'll feel like a god who can shrug off entire armies. Other times you're redoing a base or boss fight multiple times because the game offers you no meaningful way to not be hit. Hiding behind cover barely ever works and some sections (boss fights especially) offer you little cover to use. You feel like you're made of paper if you step out of cover for even a second in some areas.

- Not only that, but the gunplay is very... weak. A lot of the weapons feel very samey, and certain weapons (assault rifles and SMGs) feel like they hit like wet tissue paper. The shovel is a godsend because it can inexplicably one-hit most enemies if thrown, yet my assault rifle can't tear through a dude's helmet? I ended up using shotguns, explosives, and shovels to beat the majority of the game.

- While I can't confirm this myself because I have zero interest in the arcade, the arcade system is apparently just awful with how it manages custom maps and the UI. I've watched a few videos about it and it seems they're onto something: clunky and buggy UI seems to make it difficult to actually play a private game with a friend on a map you or they made.




Overall:

Far Cry 5 is such a conflicting experience. I see true enthusiasm and craftsmanship for this game that should be applauded after the travesty that was Primal. Yet, had I known the things I know now about how the game would turn out, I wouldn't have bought it full price.

It really boils down to the story. Gameplay wise, Far Cry 5 is solid, but the story is such a gigantic let down that it spoils the entire experience. And I can't recommend the game because of this. So it really boils down to this:


- If you want this game because of the gameplay and co-op experience, and have zero interest in being invested in the story, then I recommend it to you.

- But if you're like me and consider the story more important, then it's probably best to avoid the game until it is on sale.

[b]The Patriot simulator[/b]

I'll start with the bottom line: All in all, its 'yet another far cry game', similar to how FC3, FC4 and to some extent FC Primal look and behave.

* Story (with no spoilers) - You're playing as a deputy who tries to arrest a cult leader that has taken control of a county in Montana. This cult is made of religious extremists who believe the end is upon us and they must 'cull the herd' aka kill the weak to save the strong and be ready for 'the collapse' which is their modern version of the biblical flood i guess.
Things go to sh*t when trying to arrest him and you and your group end up in a gang-war type of scenario which you must survive till you find shelter. From there, the game actually begins just like any other FarCry game begins - You're saved by an npc that instructs you on how to start managing yourself in the map's sorroundings.
Been there, done that.

* Map - Roughly on the same size as FC3/4/Primal in terms of total size, but is much more condensed and has a lot more things to do in it. The game overall feels more of a GTA V's free roam when it comes to side-events that you find while traversing it. You will find lots of friendlies and enemies driving around and packed action is basically everywhere.
events like hostage rescue are very common, as well as helping out npc's on the road with their random problems.

* Followers - The game has added npc follower mechanic which works pretty well. You can add upto 2 specific followers with you and they can level up as they kill enemies to gain buffs. Most of these npc's are scattered across the world map and each has their own buffs, so finding new npc's as followers is a game of roulette that will either reward or screw you in terms of how good the followers will be. You have a total of 9 special followers that are story-bound, and countless of scattered npc's that can be used as random followers, which you can only 'store' up to 3 on your followers list. You can command followers to move to certain spots, kill specific enemies, and even revive you if you're dying. Long press to make them follow you again. Each follower has its own command key so they can do different things if you order them different actions.

* Guns - You can have upto 4 gun slots in your inventory (3 big weapons + 1 sidearm) + 1 slot for melee weapons + your own fists which you can use at anytime with your actual weapon (similar to Duke Nukem's kicks in the classic game Duke Nukem 3D). There are a few dozens of weapons in the game, ranging between melee weapons, pistols, smgs, rifles, snipers, and heavy guns like lmg's and rpg's.

* Skill tree - Works a bit differently than previous FC games. Its a mashup of badass ranks from Borderlands 2 and previous FC titles. Instead of steady xp gain, you get skill points on certain actions that you do, like completing missions and finishing world objectives and achievements. You spend the skill points on perks just like previous FC titles. All the ammo/holster upgrades are managed through this skill tree, so theres no more benefit in hunting animals for these kind of upgrades. Animal hides can be sold for money but that's it.

* AI - Enemy's AI seems to have a small improvement from earlier FC titles. They will take more time to detect you and their aim wont be as punishing as previous FC titles (tested on the hardest difficulty). Follower's AI can be wonky at times, but overall its tolerable.

* Arcade mode - An added minigame that lets you play with and against other people in 6v6 matches or in co-op mode against AI enemies like zombies/aliens/humans. There is also a feature that lets you build your own levels and play other people's levels.

* Uplay - The obvious elephant in the room - This game has some issues with Steam, even if you buy it directly from Steam, since it forces you to have Uplay installed and tells you to create a Uplay account for it anyway. From my experience, there are a few issues while playing this game that you should be aware of, though your milage may vary:

1) When opening and then closing the steam overlay in mid game, there is a slight chance (of about 20%-30%) that the mouse will stop responding. This has been confirmed to only happen in this game so its not a mouse issue. If this happens to you, tab out of the game and tab back in to fix it.
2) The more annoying issue: When pressing shift+f2 to bring up the Uplay interface (the equalevant of the Steam interface), there is a good chance the windows' mouse cursor will appear (and stay stuck) in the middle of the screen until you quit the game (will start happening after leaving uplay's interface and going back into the game). The only proper fix i've found for this is to restart the game. Sometimes, switching to 'borderless' mode instead of 'full screen' helps, but its not a guarantee.
3) You cant rebind the tab button, which means that if pressing tab in mid game, it will always pause the game and switch to the map view. Sounds nice, but since you can't rebind it, you have to put up with constant game interruptions if you want to shift+tab to the Steam overlay while already in a game menu, as doing this will unpause your game in the process. In other words, you will have to be aware to not be in an in-game menu screen when tabbing into the steam overlay.

Im fairly suspicious that these 3 issues are caused deliberatedly by Ubisoft to make Steam users avoid playing the game via the Steam interface and encourage them to migrate into Uplay entirely.

* Performance - The game runs at an avg of 80 fps in high-ultra settings at 1440p with Radeon RX 5700XT GPU and Ryzen 5 2600x CPU. No big frame drops seemed to appear and its overall well optimized in my opinion.


[b]As for the DLC's...[/b]


Lost on Mars - A 6-7 hours campaign that puts you on Mars with Hurk. This is a really nice DLC with incredible graphics and superb futuristic weapon designs. Lots of action packed and overall highly recommended.

Hours of Darkness - A 3.5-4 hours campaign that puts you on a Vietnam rescue mission. This DLC is quite disappointing as the objectives are very generic with no real incentive to explore the map. Its also fairly easy with the weapons they give you from the beginning. No sense of progress and all in all it feels really rushed.

Living Dead Zombies - A very short 1.5 hours gameplay that is split between 7 micro stories that Guy Marvel is trying to form about (yet another) zombie apocalypse. You play the role of the hero in each of these stories and basically he forms them while you traverse it from the world he's building around you, similar to Borderlands 2's DLC with Tiny Tina (but with zero character build up). The DLC shows how Guy Marvel is trying to pitch 7 ideas to different producers for them to build a movie from.
This is the most disappointing DLC of the bunch as it offers by far the least amount of content and priced the same as the rest. Give it a hard pass.

So, which FarCry 5 version should you buy?
The basic one. Period. I've bought the Gold one as i thought the 3 DLC's will give me lots of extra hours to grind on each, but the reality was that only the Mars DLC was worth it, both in terms of length and gameplay/story. Some other things i've recieved were free cosmetics and a few extra weapons and cars that pretty much screamed 'pay to win', alongside some fancy cosmetics. Since in game money isn't a big issue in the game, i simply can't recommend buying the gold version for these extra gadgets as you can buy them later on from vendors anyway.
So to sum it up: Buy the base game and the mars DLC individually, when they're on sale. Pass on the rest.


In summary:
As said in the beginning, when you boil it all up, its basically 'more FarCry', which comes with all the good and some of the bad of the previous titles. So if you loved playing the recent FarCry games, you will sure love this, but it doesn't seem to add anything that is new to the formula.

Before we start,

If you like to revive a dog with belly rubs,
BUY THIS GAME!

If you are not much into dogs, well, may god forgive your soul and I feel every game has Pros and Cons. Farcry 5 is not an exception. It definitely has certain pros and cons compared to its own franchise as well as many other open world games.
I have played 105 hours on PC platform as of now, in which I have completed the story mode with most of the side missions, played arcade for about 20 hours and started New Game+ with Infamous Difficulty about 20 hours ago. Uh, I mean, Farcry 5.

About performance, I have read that there were many bugs and glitches when the game was launched. I started playing about a couple of weeks ago and I did not find it as faulty as I read about it. [b]Warning:[/b] 
The single player shop requires an internet connection. If their servers are down or anything like it you won't be able to spend your *ingame money*. This is a side effect of adding microtransactions to a single player game.

[h1] Graphics and music.[/h1] 
Really good. No complaints! All the artists working on this game did an amazing job (except the writers, but more on that later).

[h1]Gameplay.[/h1] 
Combat feels great. There are some platforming sections, which are pretty good and don't overstay their welcome. You do end up driving around a little too much for my taste. I just wish fights lasted longer. You run out of targets too quickly.

In my opinion, FC5's map is the best in the series. It does feel like a rural area where people live and work.

I think weapons could have been more varied, there are many versions of the same item (long barrel, short barrel, short stock, etc.) that could have been mods. And there are probably just as many basic weapons as there are ridiculously colorful, "special" versions (Blood Dragon sniper rifle, a golden 1911 with an eagle on it, etc.). A deeper weapon customization system could have been great. I didn't expect the different ammo types, though. Those were cool.

The very, very simple crafting system for explosives and the like is welcome. I don't appreciate overcomplicated crafting in a shooter. I do not miss Far Cry 3's ridiculous wallet crafting.

I liked the non-human companions (dog, cougar, bear) and the dude on a plane. They made the game feel a little more varied. Cheeseburger (the bear) soaks up a ton of damage, Peaches (the big cat) is amazing at stealth murder, and Boomer (the dog) spots bad guys. Now if only these animals would ride in your car with you...

[h1] Kidnappings.[/h1] 
However, as much as you may enjoy the gameplay, it'll be interrupted 9 times. You will be kidnapped in an aggravating fashion with no way to stop or evade it, and it will result in often lame story missions that break up the experience.
It feels like the game punishes you for playing.

[h1] Monologues.[/h1] 
After and/or during said missions you'll have to listen to annoying and quite frankly moronic monologues by the game's antagonists. And oh boy, do they love their monologues. You have to sit there and listen to these people saying stupid sh*t in an attempt to justify their horrible cultish acts. The game acts like you're in the wrong sometimes, but it's just poor writing. You're an agent of the law doing your job and defending the innocent (ACAB aside since it's fiction), and the villains have nothing to stand on in spite of the game trying to make you look like the bad guy/gal.

Throughout the game I wanted so hard to punch the monologuing villains in the face until they died. But alas, you're not the real protagonist in this story, the writers' terrible characters are.

[h1] Actual plot.[/h1] 
There's no real theme to the game. There's no moral to the story, nothing being learned. If the writers thought they were teaching the player a lesson, I doubt they even knew what said lesson was. Far Cry 5 has no idea what it wants to say, and it ends up saying nothing of value at all while repeatedly taking away player agency.

It feels preachy (and I don't mean the religious cult characters, I mean the game itself), but it doesn't respect the player's freedom to make choices. All the "screw ups" (if they even are screw ups) are plot points the player has no choice in.

Nitpicking a little deeper, it's clear the story makes no sense from the get go. Why can't people leave the county? There are countless planes and helicopters. Why can't they retake their homes? There are endless weapons and it seems every inhabitant is a fighter. Surely a cult that came from somewhere else wouldn't have seventy-f*cking-thousand soldiers, right? (Hint: they do). What does Bliss actually do? Does it turn people into zombies? Does it make them euphoric? Vulnerable to conditioning? It's ridiculously versatile. It's a plot-drug.

Speaking of conditioning, not only does brainwashing not work like that, but even in the game it's inconsistent and barely taken advantage of by the villains.

I don't usually complain about "muh realism" like this, but a game that is clearly heavily inspired by our current reality could do much better. Make the (clearly Evangelical-based) antagonists be backed by powerful people, add some CIA brainwashing specialists, include some way in which the inhabitants were disarmed...

The game is also apolitical to a fault, considering it deals with religious cults, guns, charismatic leaders, rural America, and the threat of nuclear war. (Bear in mind Ubisoft capitalized on these things when marketing the game.)
It's like Ubisoft wanted to have its cake and eat it too. They desired praise for "tackling" heavy themes, but they didn't actually want to give any opinion on them. So the result is a washed up representation of serious issues. Like a kid's cartoon version of Watchmen. 

**Spoilers ahead, obviously**

[h1] Ending.[/h1] 
[spoiler]The nukes fall. The cult predicted it correctly.

First of all: how the flying f*ck does Seed capture everyone again? You destroyed his armies and liberated almost the entire county. Is every single inhabitant in Hope County absolutely useless? (Why do they stop being useless when they change teams?)

Onto the ending itself. It's utter trash. And I say "it" because only one of them is canon, the other one resets the game state to before the final mission (as if you'd failed).

So... nuclear apocalypse. The ending isn't earned. It's either a poor attempt at edginess or a very significant failure at understanding the gaming medium (i.e.: your actions were absolutely irrelevant), not that it would have been a good ending in any other medium (because of nonexistent theming and an abysmal setup relegated to optional audios). The game has no coherent message, if any at all. The bad guys accurately predicted nuclear war and started committing unspeakable atrocities in preparation for it. Even though you stop them, your good deeds are ignored in the end. What's the point of such a narrative? At least Spec Ops: The Line did the meta commentary well. 

Far Cry 5's ending is basically: [i]"Rocks fall everyone dies"[/i]. It doesn't fit the tone of most of the game (which is all over the place), and everything you did was for absolutely nothing. Don't get me wrong, a good story can end in tragedy, but it has to be earned. It needs to be set up. It needs to fit a broad theme. Radio transmissions and answering machine messages are not enough (ask Fallout 76 about putting all your story in prerecorded messages).

To use another TT RPG term, Joseph Seed feels like a [b]GMPC[/b]: a player character played by the game master (a huge no-no, because they end up being pet characters and "Mary Sues" who steal the spotlight).

Imagine you're reading a "choose your own adventure" book, but every path goes through the same preachy chapters in which you're blamed for the words written on the pages, and then all those paths end up with "everyone dies and your actions are irrelevant". That's Far Cry 5.
[/spoiler]

Far Cry 5 is one of those rare games that I never really stopped coming back to.

A lot of people talk about Joseph Seed when discussing Far Cry 5, and for good reason, but what keeps me returning isn't just the villains. It's Hope County itself. Ubisoft created one of the most memorable open worlds I've ever explored. The forests, rivers, mountains, farms, backroads, and small towns make Hope County feel like a real place rather than just another open-world map. Even after dozens of playthroughs, I still find myself wandering off to hunt, fish, fly around in a plane, or simply drive through the countryside listening to the radio. The setting remains one of the strongest parts of the game.

The gameplay is classic Far Cry at its best. It's chaotic, unpredictable, and sometimes completely ridiculous. One minute you're quietly clearing an outpost, the next you're being attacked by a bear while a cult convoy crashes into a fuel truck and your companion somehow turns the entire situation into a war crime. Those unscripted moments never get old.

The hunting and fishing deserve more credit, too. They're simple mechanics, but they fit perfectly into the atmosphere. Some of my favorite memories aren't story missions at all—they're just spending time in the wilderness, fishing by a lake or tracking animals through the woods before heading back to fight cultists.

Speaking of the cult, Project at Eden's Gate is still one of my favorite factions in gaming. The Seeds are memorable, but what really stands out is how believable the cult feels. The sermons, the propaganda, the music, and the constant presence of Eden's Gate throughout the county create an atmosphere that few games manage to achieve. Hope County genuinely feels occupied. The cult isn't just an enemy faction; it's part of the world's identity.

And then there's the music.

"We Will Rise Again" and "Help Me Faith" are still among my favorite tracks in any video game soundtrack. The cult choir songs are beautiful, unsettling, and strangely catchy at the same time. Years later, I still find myself listening to them outside the game. Very few soundtracks become this closely tied to a game's identity, but Far Cry 5's absolutely does.

Is the game perfect? No. Some story moments can be frustrating, and the forced captures are still controversial. But despite its flaws, Far Cry 5 has something that many technically better games don't: a personality that sticks with you.

I've played through it more than 20 times, and every time I leave Hope County, I eventually find myself coming back.

For me, that's the highest compliment I can give a game.

The best Far Cry game I've played, meaning:

-It's extremely repetitive, but takes much longer than one would expect before it begins to become tiresome.
-Plot makes absolutely 0 sense and relies entirely on contrived, magic knockout McGuffin juice to transition the player character between cutscenes and set-pieces, but no one actually cares, because this is Far Cry, and Far Cry is 99% about stabbing necks, and only 1% about showing off goofy lunatic villains giving charismatic monologues before the player character makes their 14th miraculous escape from an otherwise garunteed execution due to the aforementioned villain's neglegence and narcissism.
-Some of the minor frustrations from previous games are now gone or made less irritating, and the game has a few underwhelming, but still welcome new features, making it feel less like a totally new and innovative experience, and more like a better-polished 5th attempt at the exact same project (6th if you count regressing to being a caveman).
-The microtransactions and premium currency are indeed present in the game, but almost everything can be unlocked with sufficient grinding that only feels like being told by your mom to rake your neighbors' yard every day for five cents to save up enough money to buy a new Tech Deck, which isn't super disappointing after all, because by the time you save up a few dollars, you'll realize that Tech Decks are stupid and your interest has moved on to better things.

On a purely negative note, they didn't do that for the "deploy parachute" command, which means you'll die at least 40 times pressing the button to do so, only to shatter your femurs when the spacebar prompt fills only 30% the way up.

After a trip back into prehistory, the open-world antics of this beloved but faltering series return with Far Cry 5, and this time around, we're going to a rather unexpected location in America's 

Despite (or perhaps because of) its reputation as a backwoods area filled with hillbillies and covered wagons, there are areas of the state that very much feel like they belong in a video game or horror movie franchise.

We've had the Freemen, the Unabomber, a serial killer cannibal, religious colonies where boys and girls can't sit on the same side of the classroom, animals that can and will eat you, an annual festival for consuming fried bull testicles, an extreme gun fetish, lots of wide open space, and racking up double-digit DUIs is basically our state sport.

There has been a tonal shift from the last few games over to Far Cry 5, and that tone is found everywhere from inventory item descriptions to quest objectives to one-liners quipped by your guns for hire. In a very tried-and-true Montanan way, my hireling saw me harvesting a plant to use for a recipe and exclaimed, "Oh no, are you a vegan?"

There are loads of jokes in the inventory screen as you scroll through various items and pelts, from "oregano" that comes in a plastic baggie and is oddly good when baked in brownies to quips about sexy momma cougars.

Although not mentioned by name, Trump gets made fun of -- a lot -- so if that sort of thing is going to tick you off, well, you've been warned. I had a good chuckle when my gun for hire, whose home was recently destroyed and overrun by a cult, stated out of the blue that "last week the only thing I was worried about was the president starting a nuclear war over Twitter."

From custom-painted death tractors (yes, it is very satisfying to run cultists over with those whirling blades) to an unironic look at the doomsday prepper lifestyle, you can bet you will be constantly laughing while playing.

That's just one half of the equation of this well-rounded experience, though, as horror makes up the other side of the Far Cry coin. Although nothing overtly supernatural has happened so far in my playthrough, there are a lot of similarities to the opening segments of Outlast 2 and Resident Evil 7.

The game has some freedom to go in that direction with the psychedelic aspects brought on by a flower used in a local drug. Even plague-style "zombies" who are addicted to the stuff and shrug off gunfire make an appearance. A very strong Outlast vibe appears when antagonist Faith Seed  spouts creepy religious proclamations over the radio after completing quests in her area of the map. Based on these encounters, it's easy to see how the DLC will involve martians and zombies.

You can't help but get a little bit of a Covenant family feel along the lines of Clive Barker's Undying when seeing framed pictures of the Seed family clan. Joseph Seed himself is maybe even a better, more crazy-eyed villain than fan-favorite Vaas. The guy is legitimately unnerving, singing hymns softly to himself while staring at you all bug-eyed and getting ready to kill people.

So with this shift in tone, can you expect the exact same ride as in Far Cry 4 and Primal? The repetitive nature of the series is frequently the biggest complaint fans have, and it's clear the developers know that.

I laughed out loud near the beginning of the game when a character says, "I know what you are thinking, but don't worry, I won't be having you climb radio towers all over the county." They know about those fan complaints, and they are openly making fun of themselves.

That being said, there are plenty of familiar mechanics at play here, like hunting animals, gathering plants, liberating outposts, a vehicle chase sequence, etc., but this one feels different in a way that Far Cry 4 and Far Cry Primal didn't.

By tweaking a few elements and changing up the appearance of several key objects, this does feel like a reinvigorated version of the franchise. When you throw in the horror and resistance elements, it's sort of like Far Cry meets Homefront meets Outlast, rather than Far Cry Part 87.

The various missions, side quests, and points of interest to discover feel more organic and less like a checklist to tick off across a map. A revamped skill system features perk points gained by playing in different ways and exploring different areas, so it encourages you to vary your experience.

Far Cry 5 is also more immediately open than previous games, which typically gated you into certain areas. After completing the tutorial island, you can immediately jump in a plane and go anywhere you want, even if it's not to the next mission section. 

Resistance members can be recruited to go on missions with you, but the big draw here is the three different "fangs" for hire, offering stealth, tank, and scouting options. You have to actually work to recruit and gain the trust of these animal companions, unlike in Far Cry 4, where you could just unlock a skill and, for some reason, elephants would let you ride them into battle.

Having wild cougars and bears as your buddies is already ludicrous, though, so it's a damn shame there wasn't a bald eagle companion to help spread a little freedom.

Apart from the animal hirelings, the Far Cry formula gets changed up by creating your own maps in Arcade mode, and progression is shared between Arcade and the main story, with many perks working in both modes. You can expect to get a lot of extra hours out of the game with Arcade, either before or after completing the main story.

Far Cry is a series that has radically changed locations and environments between games, and that continues here with the switch from India to pre-historic Europe and now to Montana. Just how authentic did they make the experience, though? Pretty darn, it turns out.

The opening vignette with a camera crew interviewing people about the events of the game feels a lot like Montana. People in dingy bars at 11:00 in the morning would say those things and dress that way, and the locations mostly look spot-on.

Ubisoft got a lot right with the topography, the wildlife, the apple and pumpkin orchards, the Testy Festy, and so on. The forest and water areas are pretty accurate, although I was surprised by the rivers. While there are plenty of placid lakes for fishing, the rivers here are not nearly as calm as portrayed. They flow, and they flow fast.

Every year someone drowns trying to swim across the Missouri, which is a uniformly bad idea, so it's kind of silly seeing the deputy main character be able to do that without breaking a sweat. That's just one of those areas where a player has to suspend disbelief to have fun, though.

The climate is a bit of a stretch as well, as there's only a very small window where the state isn't either a frozen wasteland or a smoke-choked hellscape due to the summer wildfires.

The game's rip-roaring Dukes Of Hazard car chase shenanigans are fun, although that's more of a Southern thing. The menu music is also more Southern -- like almost Civil War-Southern, where you expect Ken Burns to start narrating over it -- than anything you'd typically hear in Montana. 

Yeah, by and large, we are a bunch of backward, gun-obsessed, religious hillbillies, but we're a different breed of backward, gun-obsessed, religious hillbillies than those folks down South.

Familiar mechanics, tone shift, and revamped location aside, there are some negatives here, most notably with regard to the bugs.
There were a few sections where the sound cut out for some reason, and if you stand still while talking to an NPC
Game is fine. I don't like the ubisoft client and valve should have balls big enough to tell the vendors no 3rd party clients.

[h1] Far Cry® 5[/h1]

I'm going to be honest about this right away, I never really followed the Far Cry series at all, I don't know why. But I can assure you this,  Far Cry 5 really changes my mind about it, it's so damn good. I have about 8.7 hours, I played this all in one sitting, yes I sat on my rear playing this game for that long, that's how hooked I was with it. I could've gone longer but sleep was needed. Anyways, with this review you don't have to worry much about spoilers, I'll try my best to limit the spoilers.

[h1]Storyline/Cutscenes[/h1]

The introduction of the game really was tense for me, in a good way. I'm still completing the story as I'm not halfway yet with 8.7 hours on record as I type this. The characters are pretty interesting to me too, actually rememberal to me. The setting where the Story takes place is just perfect. The Valley of this part of Montana is isolated, no help is coming for you. The way they executed this was solid in my opinion, makes the whole map basically an 'island' of some sort. How to progress through the story is likely just any Far Cry game I'm guessing. You have your main story quests and side-quests to complete, including Liberating outpost's and taking down the cult's cargo on the Montana country roads.

Your Character is now also a mute, but it's good because you can choose to be a male or female.

[h1]Performance and Graphics[/h1]

The game is optimized, certainly. I'm even shocked I'm able to run this game with just an FX-8320 CPU paired with an RX 480 8GB GPU. I'm running fair frames at around 40-60 on average with Ultra settings, nothing else changed. I notice the drops, but It's expected for me to have some lower frames at those settings in dense area's.

The graphics look solid to me, however, some people don't like them, and define them [i]Outdated, like 10 years ago[/i]. I don't see how or why it even matters. I do understand Graphics in a way do matter, but seeing 4k gameplay of this, it's beautiful without a doubt, even with me playing at 1080p. The vegetation, and atmosphere, the scenery, in general, is really good. Though, the only bad thing I saw were some ugly textures, but I'm not picky honestly, they were easy to look over as everything else looks good.

[h1]The Progression[/h1]

I do believe the Progression process occurs the same as the old Far Cry titles went. You liberate other settlements and you get them to join you. In Far Cry 5, you can also recruit people to join you, you don't have to go alone, even in Single Player.

You have perks again, like in other Far Cry's, you can use these to your advantage, it'll make life easier for you anyways by purchasing these with skill points.

Purchasing things like more guns and vehicles will also make life easier for you. You also hunt and fish, yes, fish for skins and so on to trade for money.

Special secret stashes to unlock or find. I'm not sure if these were new or not with the older Far Cry's. Basically, you have these stashes with little puzzles to solve, usually have a lot of cash to take or guns.

No need to keep going up and down with Tower's to reveal stuff on the map, the game even makes a joke of it at the beginning of it. So yes, this was cool to me, I hated it in Far Cry 3 in my opinion. 

[h1]Weapons and Vehicles.[/h1]

[u]The Weapons[/u]
There's a decent amount of weapons to unlock, you purchase them and you can equip them with upgrades such as Red Dot sights, Magazine Extension, Suppressors, and paint job finishes for your guns. You have LMG's, SMG's, Pistol's of course. There's also specials with Rocket Launchers.

You also have throwable explosives and non-explosives. These can also be craftable once you collected the right amount of stuff you need to craft them. You have your Grenades, Dynomite, and Throwing knives.

You can also throw and hit people with shovels, it's so god damn pleasing. I did this for the first 3 hours of my gameplay, no joke.

[u]The Vehicles[/u]
There's also a good fair amount of vehicles to pick from, American ones too. Do you want to drive a Semi-Truck with LMG's attached to the front of it? Hell yeah, America!

Jokes aside, there's a fair amount of vehicles you can unlock with missions, and others are purchasable. You have your Muscles cars, Jeep's with LMG's, sedans, helicopters and Airplanes, yes, airplanes. You also have boats and Jet Ski's to drive.

Also you can throw Beer can's out of your Vehicles. I don't know why but, lol. It's a challenge for me to yet hit anyone with any, but some day I'll do it.

[h1]Other Activities[/h1]

There are also little things you can do to avoid beating the hell out of the cult and causing their life hell.

You can go fishing. It's actually quite relaxing too. It takes a bit to get used to, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be scoring fish in no time.

Hunting is back, for cougars to black bears, and skunks out of nowhere spraying you for no damn reason. They also removed the animation where you cut into the animal for skins, which is a good thing and a bad thing in my opinion. But overall it makes gameplay faster, so it's understandable, or they just got lazy. Either way depends on how you look at it I guess.

Stunt events, I do believe, I don't have confirmation of what they are, but they are Vehicle related events you can choose to take part of. There are also unlockable Vehicles with Stunt related cosmetics to it such as a Trophy Truck, so I'm guessing that's how you unlock them by just doing these events.
[i]I'll update this as I'll give this a try later tonight.[/i]

[h1]The Micro-Transactions[/h1]

I don't get why people are still shocked about this like they've been living under a rock. This is Ubisoft, they've been doing this for awhile now for The Crew and Rainbow 6 Seige and other games from other companies.

Another thing to add, they don't force you to buy it, you can earn the cash with at least 15 to 30 minutes of gameplay, I don't see the issue. The alternative currency is for people who just don't want to wait, which seems stupid to me, they're paying to get something without even playing the game they bought to earn it.

I don't like the thought of micro transactions, that's why I refuse to pay for any alternative currency. 

[h1]My Final Thoughts[/h1]

The game is better than what I expected to be. I know it's changing a bit from the older Far Cry's but in my opinion, this is good, like very good. Although people are taking this game to more of the Political side more than just playing the game, which is understandable, I see some references, I define it humorous anyways in a good way and not lose my sane over it.

The Graphics are good, along with the optimization. The Story seem's average, though, can't say how it end's either because I'm not even 40% done with 8.7 hours going to 9. There's just a lot of things that are distracting to me, such as hunting and liberating outpost's that need help. Vehicle selection is decent along with weapons, although I could ask for more attachments and customization, oh well, it's better than nothing. 

I love this game, I don't know why. I would recommend, especially on sale.

Living the American Dream.

This Review is also excluding parts of the DLC that have been released, which I'm not much interested in playing.

10/10 Bass Pro Shops Simulator

[h1]The short of it:  [/h1]
There were some moments of fun to be had while playing co-op, but this is the last Ubisoft game I ever buy sight-unseen.  FarCry 5 has the (dis)honor of being the only game I ever played whose endings are so bad they made me want a refund.

[h1]The long of it:[/h1]
FarCry 5 has Moderately fun shooter gameplay that is frequently interrupted with frustration.  The open-world exploration (when you're allowed to do it) is actually legitimately enjoyable when playing co-op with a friend.  Unfortuantely, it frequently gets interrupted by magic-wielding bad guys.  Yes, that's right, I said magic.  Didn't know you were playing in the Harry Potter universe?  Well just wait until you're in the [i]cockpit of an airplane at 4000 feet[/i] and you get a magic dart in your neck after arbitrarily completing a number of objectives.  It's easily the most infuriating gameplay cock-block I've ever encountered.

What's more, the cutscenes themselves you're forced to endure are filled with some of worst "story by committee" writing I've ever seen.  With deus ex machinas and mcguffins galore, none of what happens makes any sense nor ever provides any degree of satisfaction.  I wish I'd known this going into it: [spoiler][b][u]You literally can't win the game by design.[/u][/b] The bad guy has magical fairy dust that gives him telepathic powers, astral-projection, mind control, and nuclear weapons. Your friends all die no matter what you do, and despite getting access to the ability to perform [b]aerial fucking bombardment[/b] you can never kill the cult's leader.[/spoiler]  If you've already bought it, ignore the final mission and go fishing with Cheeseburger or something instead.  Trust me, that'll be much more satisfying than the steaming turd the writers shit out of their keyboards.

In order to be "edgy" in a world supposedly "inspired by real world events," the writers should probably have considered that magical teleportation takes away from suspension of disbelief, and that villains are only scary if they make an iota of sense.  I don't know where the ball was dropped in the story, but somewhere along the line things really went tits-up in the coherency department.  None of the cult's leaders have any consistency in their beliefs or behavior, so while the voice acting and mocap are good, they all fail to make any impression except for "they're a bunch of looney tunes who are really really really bad at their job yet somehow succeed because otherwise we wouldn't have a game."

Add on microtransactions, the requirement to use the heaping pile of trash that is "UPlay," and frequent crashes that only come with "did you reboot it"-level support, I can safely say this is the least satisfied I've been with an overall game experience from a triple-A title since "Deus Ex: Invisible War."

As somebody who is unbiased from playing the other Far Cry games (This is my first one), I can say that this game is fun! If you're the type of person who likes to have heavy action, then you can charge in with helicopters, rocket launchers etc. Or if you're the type of person (like me) who loves stealth, you can modify your weapons to have silencers or go in with a bow. It definitely caters to every type of player in that regard. 

The companions are pretty cool! You can have an NPC flying above in a plane or helicopter acting as a guardian angel, or you can have a dog to sniff out enemies and a sniper planted on a rock to watch your back. 

The graphics are absolutely gorgeous! I play at max settings on a 1440p monitor and get a consistent 70-80FPS with a 3060ti and it looks unreal! The lush nature of Montana is so lovely to look at and explore. I can spend hours hunting in the woods or fishing at a lake and getting lost in the visuals. 

The story is good, but nothing special. In a nut shell, you play as a sheriffs deputy trying to take down a family of religious fanatics who have basically raised an entire army at this point. The characters have some decent depth to them and are memorable, but they're nothing groundbreaking. 

As I said at the start, I am unbiased and have not played Far Cry 3 (What everyone says is the best one) for more than around an hour in the years that I've owned it. So coming in as a newcomer to the series, I absolutely love this game.

The bones of a fine sandbox game are here. However, the devs fell in love with their own writing. In all the three territories, you experience immersion-breaking "inescapable capture" episodes in which your character is taken prisoner repeatedly through magical means and subjected to long, tedious so-called missions in which you have to sit passively watching long speeches by NPCs or are forced into surreal and frankly silly 'vision missions' that are fun for the writers and for nobody else. I had to keep walking away from this game in frustration with these trials in patience.

Far Cry 5 is a certain update to the well-known FPS serial, set into the really big and quite realistic-made open-world. The thing is, it was story-driven game previously. And now, the story is blatantly dull and uninspiring, and the main game's driver is the open-world itself and notorious Grind. Yeah, the same itch as with all the latest Ubisoft projects, like Ghost Recon Wildlands, the Division, latest Assassin Creed titles - et cetera.

Well-made open-world with dozens of various activities and possibilities to entertain yourself - sounds like a very good deal, ain't it? The fishing simulation here in Far Cry 5 is on the level with the best fishing simulator games, it is that good. The shooting and the weapon tuning, while simplified, still can attract many hours of interest for various shooting challenges. Same goes for driving and especially flying - there are some really crazy stunt challenges to perform! The world map is big, there are some different biomes, with a vast variety of flora and fauna.

The world around the player is balanced much better than it was in previous Far Cry games. However, that achievement goes with the oblivion of immersive story involvement and character development we had in Far Cry 3. Even in the controversial Far Cry 2, we had better immersion, some actual choices to make. From that point, with Far Cry 5 the player's role is simplified to a walking gun mount, which is following external orders and moves along the thin string of the puppeteer. Not even a sip of free will in all of the story plot. Your character has more scripts to obey than any enemy you'll encounter.

And the main game process is just as monotonous as any day in the office or in some factory where you have to perform the same routine tasks every day. What's the difference between work the most of us have to do for bread and beef, and the "game" which is pushing you to do all the same "quests" over and over and over? You have released some cult prisoners in the wilderness? Or from the van? Or maybe you have blown the truck with the evil weed or gasoline? Rinse and repeat. 50-100 time more. And for what special endgame goal? To unlock the next difficulty level, to play it all again, just as in the rogue-like 2-hours-through-games?

Ubisoft route ain't the one I want to follow, therefore, downvote. My mark for the game is 6/10. It's well-made in many aspects... Except for the proper immersion and entertainment.

EDIT: After playing the game to completion I feel the game more than earns it's not recommended vote from me. So, it's not just for one "small" detail about an extremely ridiculous and fundamental flaw in game design. The AI is retarded. There are bugs galore. It's just the same old nonsensical Farcry as every other time. Except this time, you play as a lame mute with no characterization and the ending(s) of the game just spit on you. Just stop making Farcry games Ubisoft. It doesn't seem recoverable at this point.

So, I like open world games, but not all open world games are good.  I liked this one.

Summary:
Fun gameplay, excellent character animation and visual details, beautiful world, a little bit repetitive, cars drive weird.  Better than I expected it to be.

Technically, this game is excellent.  The character animations, lighting, shadows, textures, all very well done.  The wake left in the water as you pilot watercraft stood out to me when I first noticed it.  It's not just a texture of wake, but actual waves.  I know that more recent games like Sea of Thieves does water very well, but it stood out to me.  The world in general looks fantastic.  The sky, sun, light, shadows, textures, all are good.

The freedom to do whatever, and have that contribute to the main story is both good and bad.  Good in that I can play how I like to and be able to finish the game.  Bad in that the game progresses based on a point system, and once you reach a critical point, some main story missions disappear forever.

The gameplay feels good.  The guns are fun to use, there is a good variety of weapons without any one weapon being objectively better than others.  You can have fun with any weapons you like and be able to play the game without being handicapped.  It can be repetitive to basically do the same things repeatedly in different areas, like taking over outposts.  For me, the gameplay is good enough to make up for it.  It's something I want to do because the gameplay is so enjoyable, and the different locations kind of makes each one a little bit different.

The story is okay.  I'm still not really sure how I feel about it, or what exactly I'm meant to take away from it.  It's just a little bit weird, and there are periods where control is taken away from you which was annoying and confusing at first.  However, it's a recurring theme of some sort and I accepted it.  The intro and in engine cutscenes are again very well done.  Lots of details in the characters, good lighting, and good voice acting too, I think.  The characters feel real with real emotions.  Probably a lot of expensive motion capture to do, but it's good.

There are collectables, which I'm not usually a fan of, but there are maps you can get to reveal their locations which changes it from an infuriating search to a boring chore.  All collectables can be picked up in 30 minutes after you've explored all the landmarks and can fast travel around to pick them up.

Coop multiplayer is great.  Playing with a friend is fun.

Cars drive kind of weird.  They can be floaty feeling and not as responsive as I'd like.  Especially with sportier cars, if you gun the acceleration from standstill you lose traction.  It makes sense, that happens in real live, but playing on a keyboard it's kind of annoying.  This is probably less of an issue if playing with a controller with analog triggers.  Vehicles in general behave kind of weirdly.  I would say that GTA V has the best vehicle physics for an open world game, so that's where i'm coming from.

So, there is the usual game currency, but you can also buy special currency with real money that you can use to buy special guns and clothes.  Kind of disappointing that this would be what I would consider a premium game, but anything you can buy with special currency you can buy with game currency that you earn just playing the game.  It might be a struggle to buy all of the things with game currency, but I don't want to do that anyways.  Some things I just don't care about so I don't bother with those.

The only other Farcry game I played was Primal.  I was concerned that the similar Farcry formula would make the game repetitive, but this was different enough that I really enjoyed it.  Would I play Farcry 4 after playing this?  Probably not.  Would I play New Dawn?  Not sure.

Well, after playing over 70 hours of Far Cry 5 (so far), having finished the story, played a fair amount of coop aswell the multiplayer arcade mode, I think I can give my review of Far Cry 5.

So first of, is the game any good? Well the simple answer is yes, its pretty good. 

The world is beautiful and has an insane amount of detail. It genuinely feels real, believable and lived in. Moving from the more exotic survival locations of previous games to a setting with houses and people living their normal lives works well and feels like a refreshing change to the far cry formula (although its not a setting I would like them to use again). A lot of the animations from FC3 and 4 have been changed and the movement feels a lot faster and more fluid. No slow clunky climbing and volting animations anymore. The gunplay feels better than ever, and a lot of weapons have been tuned and balanced to make them work better in this game. The bow for example can now shoot much further away and is much more accurate, which makes it a much more viable weapon for stealth / sniper builds.

The game has four villains, one main one and three sub bosses you must kill before you can fight the main boss. Overall the bosses are alright, but not as good as Vaas or Pagan Min IMO, bit still a huge step up from Primal (I can't even remember the main villains name in that game).

Missions can now be played in any order and the world is divided into 3 regions, each containing its own sub story that contributes to the over all story. The pacing can feel abit weird in some places, going from a mission about innocent people being tortured to the next mission being about collecting cow testies for the local testie festie (Im not joking) and some of the story missions can get a bit repetitive. Overall, the story is ok, better than I expected but still not as good as 3 or 4 in my opinion, although far cry games have never really had stories that are that great to be honest. Ubisoft really need to sort out their story telling after AC Origins terrible story and FC5's mediocre one, but that's a debate for another day.

The repetitive survival aspects like collecting animal skins and different coloured leaves to make syringes have been removed. There is no looting / collecting / skinning animations any more making the game less of a grind, and improving your gear is now done through the skills menu instead of "collect XYZ animal skins" to make something. Animals are much easier to kill now so if you liked the challenge of taking down a mountain bear in FC4 then you might not like it so much here. The emphasis is more focused on the cult your fighting against and less on the environment trying to kill you, which some may love but others may hate.

They have also overhauled the side content in a similar way to what they did with assassin's creed, moving away from the repetitive hostage rescue and assassination missions, to unique and interesting side missions with developed characters and fun objectives. Most of the fun comes from the side missions IMO, especially in coop.

The game also has an arcade mode, where the map editior from previous games make a comeback, only this time you can use assets from Far Cry 5, 4, Primal, AC 4 Black Flag, AC Unity and Watch Dogs 1 to make your maps. It is much more in depth this time and you can make your own objectives and gamemodes and tweak a lot of stuff to make it play the way you want. This means there is a lot more choice when making maps, and the multiplayer in this game works by allowing players to vote for a community made map and you play it the way the creator made it to be played. This can mean that the multiplayer can be very unbalanced and even sometimes broken, and there are not many good maps that have been made so far, but with Ubis promise to keep updating it and as more time passes, im sure more good maps will be made and the multiplayer will become a lot more fun and balanced.

The game also has full 2 player coop now which unlocks after the first 1 hour, so you can now play through the entire story with a friend which is awesome. It works pretty well and I haven't had any disconnection issues or any major problems with it. The only main issue is that progress only saves for the host, so you will need to play with someone who has already played a lot of the game for it to work well, but since I already beat most of the game before trying the coop it wasn't an issue for me.

This game also feels like it borrows a lot from other Ubisoft games. The new side quest system from ACO is here, a lot of the customisation and the ability to lean out if vehicles to shoot feels like its been borrowed from GR Wildlands and I'm pretty sure the animation for climbing through windows has been stolen from R6:Siege. These are not necessarily bad things but for people who think a lot of ubi games feel similar you might not like this game all that much.

Now although this game beat my expectations and has make a lot of good improvements to the franchise, it still has a few things that aren't so good and it doesn't quite live up to FC4 (my fav far cry) in my opinion, and here are a few reasons why:

The game has two main endings, both of which are pure trash in my opinion. I don't want to go into spoilers for you, but all I can say is that both ending are not satisfying at all which is a huge let down to what is otherwise a really good game.

The dumbing down of the survival aspects also rubbed me the wrong way since far cry has always been a survival franchise. I'm not really sure if this game deserves to have far cry in the name. I'm not saying that its a bad game, just that its not the best far cry game.

The gameplay still plays very similar to FC3, 4, Primal, Blood dragon etc despite the changes they made to the animations, and the franchise is really in need of a reboot or refresh, similar to what Ubi did with AC origins.

You now make your own character in this game instead of the usual pre defined characters from previous games. FC games have never really had likable characters so this seemed like a good step, but there are quite a few times in the story when scenes feel really awkward since your character doesn't speak and when someone asks you something, your just left with an awkward silence. I think in the next game, they should allow you to chose a voice for your character and actually have them speak, because it would make the story feel more personal and less awkward in certain parts of the story.

So overall, Far Cry 5 is a really good game. It has its fair share of issues, and if you were expecting something brand new and innovative for the franchise or a deep, emotional, gripping story then you will probably feel let down. But personally, I went in with very low expectations and I was pretty happy with how this game turned out. For the most part, the things this game does new, work pretty well. I still think the Far Cry franchise is in desperate need of a major refresh or engine change but FC5 is a pretty good game, and one of my fav games released this year so far. And playing this game coop is even better.
